apidx.location: src/haute/_types.py:596 (NodeData.label); frontend/src/types/node.ts:24 (func_name) & :13 (label); src/haute/trace.py:152,794,829,969 (node_name = node_data.label); src/haute/schemas.py:316-317 (TraceStepResponse.node_name/node_type)
apidx.title: A node's display/identity has three names -- `label` (config), `func_name` (frontend/codegen), `node_name` (trace API)
apidx.description: The human-facing name of a node is referred to three ways depending on layer. Config / canonical model: `label` (NodeData.label, _types.py:596). Frontend node data + codegen: `func_name` (node.ts:24, the sanitised Python function/identifier derived from the label). Trace API response: `node_name` (TraceStepResponse.node_name, schemas.py:316), which trace.py:794 sets directly from `node_data.label` (`node_name = node_data.label`). So the trace step's `node_name` IS the `label`, but a reader of the trace contract has no way to know that `node_name`, `label`, and the frontend's `func_name` are the same underlying string (or how they relate -- node_name==label, func_name==sanitize(label)). The trace response also pairs `node_name` with `node_type` while the canonical model field is `nodeType` (camel, _types.py:598), adding a third casing twist on the same struct.
apidx.recommended_fix: Pick one term for 'node display name' (label) and one for 'node identifier/function name' (func_name) and use them consistently. In the trace surface, either rename TraceStepResponse.node_name -> label (matching the model) or document at the field that `node_name == NodeData.label` and `node_type == NodeData.nodeType`. Keep `func_name` reserved strictly for the sanitised codegen identifier and cross-reference it to `label` in node.ts. A short docstring on TraceStepResponse mapping node_name<->label<->func_name removes the ambiguity even if the rename is deferred.

apidx.location: src/haute/_types.py:336 (OptimiserConfig.scenario_index), :403 (ScenarioExpanderConfig.step_column # name of the 0-based step index column), :459 (OnlineSolveResultLike.n_steps); src/haute/_builders.py:845,863 (config.get('step_column','scenario_index')); src/haute/schemas.py:1150 (n_steps)
apidx.title: The scenario step-index concept has ~4 names: `scenario_index` (optimiser), `step_column`/`step_col` (expander/builders), `n_steps`/`steps` (counts)
apidx.description: The expander produces a 0-based step-index column and the optimiser consumes it, but they name it differently. ScenarioExpanderConfig calls the field `step_column` whose *value* is conventionally 'scenario_index' (_types.py:403 comment: 'name of the 0-based step index column (e.g. "scenario_index")'), while OptimiserConfig names the same column `scenario_index` (_types.py:336). The builder bridges them with `config.get('step_column','scenario_index')` (_builders.py:845,863) and `config.get('step_column') or 'scenario_index'` -- so the producer key is `step_column` and the consumer key is `scenario_index` for one and the same column. Internally it is then carried as the local `step_col`. Separately, the per-quote step COUNT is `steps` in the expander config (_types.py:402) but `n_steps` in the solve result (schemas.py:1150, _types.py:459). A new engineer wiring an expander -> optimiser must learn that `step_column` and `scenario_index` denote the same column and that `steps` becomes `n_steps`.
apidx.recommended_fix: Align the producer and consumer key names: rename ScenarioExpanderConfig.step_column -> scenario_index (with a read shim for old configs) so both the expander and optimiser use `scenario_index` for the column, and reserve `step` strictly for the count (`steps` config / `n_steps` result -- or rename one of those too for full symmetry). Update _builders.py and SCENARIO_EXPANDER_CONFIG_KEYS accordingly and document the expander->optimiser column contract in one place (e.g. ScenarioExpanderConfig docstring) so the linkage is explicit.

apidx.location: frontend/src/utils/nodeTypes.ts:55 (API_INPUT name 'Quote Input', label 'QUOTE IN'), :58 (OUTPUT name 'Quote Response', label 'QUOTE OUT') vs src/haute/_types.py:32 (API_INPUT='apiInput'), :39 (OUTPUT='output'); decorator @pipeline.api_input (_types.py:54)
apidx.title: Frontend product names for the entry/exit nodes ('Quote Input' / 'Quote Response') don't match the code/docs/decorator vocabulary ('apiInput' / 'output' / api_input), hurting grep-navigability
apidx.description: The two most prominent nodes are labelled in the UI with product names that share no token with their code identity. apiInput is shown as name 'Quote Input' / badge 'QUOTE IN' (nodeTypes.ts:55), but the NodeType is `apiInput` (_types.py:32), the decorator is `@pipeline.api_input` (_types.py:54), the docs/config call it apiInput, and the schema model is ApiInput*. output is shown as 'Quote Response' / 'QUOTE OUT' (nodeTypes.ts:58) but the type/decorator/config are `output`/`@pipeline.output`. A new engineer who sees 'Quote Input' in the UI and greps the backend for 'quote'/'QuoteInput' will not find the apiInput node; conversely someone reading `apiInput` in code has to know it surfaces as 'Quote Input'. (Contrast modelling: backend `modelling` vs UI 'Model Training' at least share 'model'.) This is a navigability footgun precisely where newcomers start.
apidx.recommended_fix: Either align the product label tokens with the code identity (e.g. include 'API' or 'apiInput' in a tooltip/aria description) or, better, add an explicit mapping table (node type id -> display name -> decorator) in one discoverable place (docs node reference or a comment block over NODE_TYPE_META) so 'Quote Input' is one search away from 'apiInput'. Do not rename the product label if it is intentional UX; just make the code<->UI term link explicit and greppable.

apidx.location: src/haute/schemas.py:1030 (quote_count) vs :1149 (n_quotes); src/haute/_types.py:333 (quote_id) vs frontend/src/types/trace.ts:225 (quote_id_column); frontend/src/api/types.ts:507 (quote_count) vs :652 (n_quotes)
apidx.title: Quote-count uses two names (`quote_count` in the estimate vs `n_quotes` in the solve result); quote-id appears as both `quote_id` and `quote_id_column`
apidx.description: The number of quotes is `quote_count` on OptimiserEstimateResponse (schemas.py:1030; types.ts:507) but `n_quotes` on OptimiserSolveResult (schemas.py:1149; types.ts:652). Both are 'how many quotes', surfaced by adjacent optimiser endpoints; a frontend dev must remember which response uses which spelling. Similarly the quote identifier column is the config key `quote_id` (_types.py:333) but is surfaced in the trace detail as `quote_id_column` (trace.ts:225) -- consistent with a *_column suffix pattern elsewhere, but inconsistent with the bare `quote_id` config key for the same thing. These are lower severity than the casing/output-value issues but add to the per-endpoint memorisation burden.
apidx.recommended_fix: Standardise the count name across optimiser responses -- prefer `quote_count` (reads as English; or `n_quotes` if matching the solver's n_* convention is preferred) -- and apply it to both OptimiserEstimateResponse and OptimiserSolveResult (alias the old name for one release). Adopt a single rule for the *_column suffix: if config keys that name a column use the bare concept (`quote_id`), keep trace-detail fields consistent (or document that trace details append `_column` by convention so the relationship is predictable).

apidx.location: src/haute/_types.py:315 (var_power) and :318 (variance_power) both in ModellingConfig; src/haute/modelling/_train_config.py:67-68,114-124 (both accepted, var_power wins); frontend/src/panels/modelling/TargetAndTaskConfig.tsx:126 (writes variance_power); docs/GLM_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md:62,104 (var_power) vs rating/config/model_training/avg_top_5.json:8 (variance_power)
apidx.title: The Tweedie variance power has two config keys -- `var_power` (GLM-side) and `variance_power` (CatBoost/UI-side) -- for one parameter
apidx.description: ModellingConfig declares BOTH `var_power` (_types.py:315, listed under GLM-specific) and `variance_power` (_types.py:318, under CatBoost/shared) for the single Tweedie variance-power parameter. _train_config.py merges/reconciles them (:67-68, :109-124) with `var_power` winning on conflict. The UI writes `variance_power` (TargetAndTaskConfig.tsx:126), GLM docs use `var_power` (GLM_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md:62), and on-disk configs use `variance_power` (avg_top_5.json:8). So which key a config carries depends on whether it came from the GLM path, the CatBoost path, the UI, or the docs. This is the naming half of an existing behavioral finding (candidates.json:5339 'Conflicting top-level var_power vs variance_power is silently resolved'); flagged here for the vocabulary-coherence angle, which the behavioral finding does not address.
apidx.recommended_fix: Pick one canonical key (`variance_power` is more self-explanatory and is what the UI/most configs already write) and treat the other strictly as a deprecated read alias that emits a warning, never a co-equal field. Stop declaring both as first-class in ModellingConfig -- declare the canonical one and document the alias. Align the GLM docs to the canonical name. (Coordinate with the behavioral fix in candidates.json#5339 so the silent-resolution and the dual-naming are addressed together.)

apidx.location: docs/ (30+ design docs incl. RATING_STEP_DESIGN.md, GLM_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md, optimiser-frontier-design.md, SUBMODEL_DESIGN.md) -- no GLOSSARY.md/CONCEPTS.md; vocabulary spread across src/haute/_types.py and frontend/src/utils/nodeTypes.ts
apidx.title: No single glossary defines the domain vocabulary, so overloaded terms (factor/feature/column, scenario_value/optimal_scenario_value, validation/test, label/func_name/node_name) have no authoritative meaning
apidx.description: Despite 30+ design docs under docs/, there is no GLOSSARY/CONCEPTS/TERMINOLOGY page that defines the core nouns a new engineer must learn, and the project leans on a domain-specific actuarial vocabulary (factor, banding, ratebook, lambdas, frontier) layered over a generic dataframe/ML vocabulary (column, feature, target, weight). The result is several overloaded terms with no canonical definition: 'factor' means an actuarial rating dimension (RatingTable.factors, factor_columns, BandingFactor) AND collides with ML 'feature' (feature_columns, cat_features) for what is sometimes the same column; 'scenario_value' vs 'optimal_scenario_value' vs 'optimised_factor' (see separate finding); 'test' vs 'validation'; 'label' vs 'func_name' vs 'node_name'. Each of the findings above is, at root, a missing shared dictionary. Without it the inconsistencies will keep re-accreting as new nodes are added.
apidx.recommended_fix: Add docs/GLOSSARY.md (linked from docs/index.md and ARCHITECTURE.md) that defines each core term once: node (label vs func_name vs node_name), factor vs feature vs column, premium/price/expected_income/objective, scenario_value/scenario_index and their solver/output names, train/validation/holdout, ratebook/online mode, lambdas/frontier/constraint. State the canonical config-key casing convention there too. Reference the glossary from the casing CI test (finding 1) so the conventions are enforced, not just documented.

ci-prevention.title: OpenAPI contract fingerprint is field-blind: backend schema field renames/type changes ship GREEN
ci-prevention.location: tests/test_api_contracts.py:8 (_normalise_schema), :21 (_api_contract_fingerprint), :512 (test_openapi_contract_fingerprint_matches_expected_snapshot)
ci-prevention.description: _normalise_schema() collapses every response/request to only {"$ref": ...} or {type,title}; it never follows the $ref into components/schemas, so the fingerprint is identical whether TrainResponse.glm_relativities is renamed, retyped (float->str), made optional, or dropped. The snapshot test therefore proves only that the path->ref WIRING is stable, not that any field/type the frontend consumes is stable. Combined with the fact that frontend/src/types/*.ts (node.ts, trace.ts, banding.ts, guards.ts) are hand-authored with NO generation from the schema, a backend field-level change is invisible to the entire CI. The only field-level protections are (a) the single ALLOWED_TYPES list comparison in test_frontend_backend_contract.py and (b) ~45 hand-maintained JSON fixtures in tests/fixtures/ui_contracts validated against Pydantic models in test_backend_frontend_contracts.py — both of which a developer must remember to update, so they do not detect drift, they only assert hand-written parity.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Make the backend schema the single source of truth and enforce mechanically: (1) a committed artifact (e.g. frontend/src/types/api.generated.ts) produced by exporting app.openapi() / model_json_schema() and running an OpenAPI->TS generator; (2) a CI job 'schema-sync' that regenerates the artifact and the OpenAPI JSON, then runs `git diff --exit-code` so any backend schema change that is not reflected in committed generated types fails the build; (3) delete the hand-maintained fingerprint snapshot and ALLOWED_TYPES mirror in favour of the generated diff. This dissolves the entire frontend/backend schema-drift class at field granularity.
ci-prevention.prevents: frontend/backend schema drift (field rename, type change, required/optional flip, dropped field) — the class the current fingerprint + ALLOWED_TYPES + fixtures only partially and manually cover.

ci-prevention.title: Standalone-.py portability promise is never exercised in a clean interpreter for DEPLOYED/codegen output
ci-prevention.location: tests/test_e2e.py:1 (parse->execute->codegen->re-parse all in-process); tests/test_starter_pipeline_e2e.py:519 (only the `init` scaffold runs in subprocess); .github/workflows/ci.yml:85-110 (package-smoke installs wheel but only runs package_smoke_check.py + `haute --help`)
ci-prevention.description: The portability promise ('the emitted .py runs standalone') is asserted in test_e2e.py only as an IN-PROCESS round-trip: graph_to_code() then parse_pipeline_source() in the same interpreter that already has polars/catboost/rustystats and the full repo on sys.path. The only true clean-subprocess execution is the `haute init` starter scaffold (test_starter_pipeline_e2e.py:519 shells out with sys.executable). The package-smoke CI lane installs the wheel into a fresh venv but only imports haute, checks static assets/routes, and runs `haute --help` — it never executes a real generated/deployed pipeline .py end-to-end against ONLY the wheel's runtime deps. So an emitted file that imports a dev-only or test-only symbol, relies on repo-relative paths, or depends on a transitive dep not in [project.dependencies] would still pass every gate.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a CI lane (extend package-smoke) that, inside the wheel-only venv: scaffolds or loads a representative pipeline, calls the deploy/codegen path to emit the standalone .py, then runs `./.pkg-wheel/bin/python <emitted>.py` (or `python -m pytest` on a generated test) in that clean process and asserts the printed premium matches a golden value. This proves the emitted artifact runs with only [project.dependencies] installed.
ci-prevention.prevents: standalone-.py portability regressions (missing/incorrect import in codegen output, reliance on dev-group deps, repo-relative path leakage) that in-process round-trip tests structurally cannot catch.

ci-prevention.title: No validate-vs-serve numeric parity gate for the deployed/containerized scorer
ci-prevention.location: tests/test_deploy_expected_output_validation.py (validate path only); tests/test_deploy_contract_integrity.py:1 (feature-contract + test-quote failure handling); tests/test_deploy_container.py (container build, no numeric parity grep hit)
ci-prevention.description: validate_deploy()/score_test_quotes() and the feature-contract guard are well tested, and the container build is tested, but no test asserts that the SERVED/containerized scorer returns byte-identical (or within-tolerance) numbers to the in-editor execute_graph()/validate path for the same quote. The 'deploy validate passed but serve returns different numbers' class (feature-order skew, missing artifact substitution at serve time, contract drift between bundle and runtime) is exactly the seam between the two code paths and is the one not pinned.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a parity test: take a golden quote, compute the premium via the in-editor execute path AND via the deployed scorer entrypoint (the same callable the container/serve route invokes), assert equality within the documented tolerance. Run it in the wheel-only venv lane so it doubles as deploy-portability coverage.
ci-prevention.prevents: deploy validate-vs-serve divergence (the served artifact silently producing different numbers than validation approved).

ci-prevention.title: Coverage gates measure line/branch reachability, not behaviour; mutation (the behavioural gate) is path-filtered and not required on main
ci-prevention.location: .github/workflows/mutation.yml:6-12 (PR trigger filtered to src/haute/**/*.py, tests/**, mutation/**); scripts/run_mutation_suite.py:304 (_select_targets_for_changed_files skips when no mutation-relevant file changed); pyproject.toml:158 fail_under=90 + [tool.haute.critical_coverage]
ci-prevention.description: The 90% global + per-file critical coverage gates prove lines/branches are EXECUTED, not that an assertion would fail if the behaviour changed — a test can import-and-touch a critical module (parser.py, executor.py, _model_scorer.py) for coverage credit without asserting correctness. Mutation testing is the only behavioural gate, but: (1) it runs only on PRs whose diff touches src/haute/**/*.py or tests/** (a change to e.g. pyproject thresholds, a config JSON, or codegen template data files that affects behaviour but not those globs runs zero mutants); (2) on a direct push to main mutation.yml's pull_request trigger does not fire, so a force-merge or admin push lands with no mutation check; (3) mutation is a separate workflow, so unless branch protection lists it as required, a PR can merge while it is queued/failing.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: (a) Add a small always-on mutation smoke (a handful of highest-value mutants on parser.py/executor.py/_model_scorer.py) to the blocking CI 'backend' lane so every change pays a behavioural check; (b) document/enforce that mutation.yml is a REQUIRED status check in branch protection; (c) broaden the mutation path filter to include codegen template/data and config files that influence pricing behaviour.
ci-prevention.prevents: coverage-gaming silent wrongness (lines covered, behaviour unverified) and parse->codegen->execute equivalence regressions slipping past line-coverage when the diff dodges the mutation path filter.

ci-prevention.title: Perf and mutation lanes do not gate pushes to main; perf has no committed baseline so it only catches absolute-budget blowups, not regressions
ci-prevention.location: .github/workflows/performance.yml:4-6 (workflow_dispatch + weekly cron only); .github/workflows/ci.yml:35-54 (PR perf lane runs run_perf_suite but gates only on absolute budgets); scripts/run_perf_suite.py:59 (_budget_violations compares against fixed max_total/max_test seconds, no baseline delta)
ci-prevention.description: The standalone performance.yml workflow is cron/dispatch only — it never runs on PRs or main pushes, so it cannot block a merge. The PR-time perf lane in ci.yml IS blocking but run_perf_suite only fails on absolute budget violations (max-total/max-test seconds) and on skipped/xfailed perf tests; there is no committed performance baseline and no per-test regression-vs-baseline delta. A change that doubles a hot path's time but stays under the 120s per-test ceiling ships GREEN. Artifacts are uploaded but nothing consumes the previous run to compute a delta.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Commit a perf baseline (per-test medians) and make the PR perf lane fail when a test regresses beyond a tolerance vs baseline (ratchet), not only when it exceeds an absolute ceiling; regenerate the baseline deliberately like the test-debt budget. Optionally run the perf lane on main pushes too so the baseline tracks merged state.
ci-prevention.prevents: silent performance regressions within the absolute budget; perf coverage being merged without ever running (cron-only workflow).

ci-prevention.title: Cache-integrity invariants are unit-tested but there is no cross-process / concurrent-writer durability lane
ci-prevention.location: tests/test_json_cache_integrity.py:1-16 (single-process, in-test concurrency via threads at :259); .github/workflows/ci.yml (no dedicated cache-integrity / concurrency lane; backend runs the suite under -n workers with --timeout-method=signal on POSIX)
ci-prevention.description: Cache integrity (schema-fingerprint vs content-hash arbitration, atomic temp-dir promotion, stale-mirror prevention) is covered by strong single-process tests using in-process threads. But the real failure mode is multi-PROCESS: two `haute` invocations or a serve worker + a CLI rebuild racing on the same .cache directory, and crash-during-promote durability. Thread-based tests share a GIL and an interpreter and cannot reproduce OS-level rename/lock races or a killed process mid-write. There is also no Windows leg for the cache-integrity suite specifically (platform-smoke runs path/debt/file_ops tests, not test_json_cache_integrity.py), yet the atomic-write reader-contention debt entries in test_test_debt.py (08c3e550, 716bebf0) show Windows rename semantics differ.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a cross-process cache durability test (spawn 2+ subprocesses contending on one cache dir; kill one mid-promote; assert the survivor reads a consistent, non-stale parquet and the killed write leaves no half-promoted layer) and include test_json_cache_integrity.py + the new cross-process test in the windows-latest platform-smoke matrix so rename/lock divergence is gated on the OS that actually differs.
ci-prevention.prevents: cache-integrity corruption under concurrent processes / crash-during-write, and Windows-specific cache races, which the current GIL-bound thread tests cannot exercise.

ci-prevention.title: mkdocs --strict (docstring/cross-reference breakage) only runs on docs/** path pushes, not on PRs that edit rendered docstrings
ci-prevention.location: .github/workflows/docs.yml:3-8 (push to main filtered to docs/** and mkdocs.yml; no pull_request trigger)
ci-prevention.description: docs.yml builds with --strict (which fails on broken mkdocstrings references) but only triggers on push to main when docs/** or mkdocs.yml changed. mkdocstrings renders Python docstrings from src/haute/**, so a PR that breaks a cross-reference or an autodoc target in a module docstring will NOT trigger docs.yml (the path filter excludes src/**), and the main backend CI never runs mkdocs. The broken docs build is only discovered after merge, on the main push — and only if that same push happened to touch docs/**.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a pull_request trigger to docs.yml (build-only, no deploy) OR add `uv run mkdocs build --strict` to the blocking backend preflight, so docstring/reference breakage in src/** is caught pre-merge.
ci-prevention.prevents: post-merge docs build breakage from src/** docstring/reference changes that the docs path filter currently lets through.

ci-prevention.title: Backend CI matrix tests 3 Python versions only on Linux; package-smoke, deploy, and contract lanes are single-version single-OS
ci-prevention.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml:16-18 (matrix 3.11/3.12/3.13 ubuntu only), :85-110 (package-smoke 3.12 ubuntu only), :112-128 (platform-smoke runs only a 4-file path/debt subset on win/mac)
ci-prevention.description: The full backend suite + coverage gates run across 3.11/3.12/3.13 but only on ubuntu-latest. platform-smoke on windows/macos runs ONLY tests/test_path_resolution.py, test_pipeline_runtime_path_validation.py, test_test_debt.py, test_file_ops.py — so the parser/executor/codegen/scorer/deploy/cache behaviour is never executed on Windows or macOS in CI, despite the codebase carrying explicit Windows-specific branches (npm.cmd resolution in hatch_build.py:117-124 and cli helpers, MoveFileExW rename semantics, drive-letter pyvenv guards in both preflight scripts). package-smoke (wheel/sdist install + standalone) runs only on 3.12/ubuntu, so a wheel that fails to install or run on Windows or on 3.11/3.13 ships green.

ci-prevention.title: No execution-level parse->codegen->execute differential harness: structural roundtrip passes while standalone VALUES diverge
ci-prevention.location: tests/test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py (structural-only); tests/test_pipeline.py (executor-only); src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:784-858 (_make_passthrough_builder + liveSwitch _gen_live_switch:522)
ci-prevention.description: The capstone roundtrip property test asserts ONLY (a) parse(codegen(g)) preserves representable semantics and (b) codegen(parse(codegen(g))) is byte-identical source. Its own docstring budgets execution out. Separately, test_pipeline.py exercises p.run()/p.score() but on the in-memory Pipeline object built from the DSL -- i.e. it runs the EXECUTOR path, never a codegen-emitted file reparsed and executed standalone. The result: _make_passthrough_builder emits `return {first}` for OPTIMISER, OPTIMISER_APPLY, MODELLING, SCENARIO_EXPANDER (confirmed at _codegen_builders.py:847-858), and _gen_live_switch hard-routes the 'live' input, so the generated standalone file performs a no-op / wrong-branch where the executor applies real logic. Every current gate is green; the saved pipeline mis-prices when run outside the canvas. This is the architecture's #1-ranked risk (semantic equivalence, heat-map score 10) and is currently unguarded at the value level.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add tests/test_codegen_execute_differential.py: for a corpus graph covering frozenset(NodeType) - {SUBMODEL, SUBMODEL_PORT} (reuse the capstone _capstone_root_graph fixture), do graph_to_code_multi(g) -> write to tmp -> write sidecars -> load the standalone module and call pipeline.run() (source=batch) and pipeline.score(df) (source=live) -> assert_frame_equal against execute_graph(g) for each output node, for BOTH source values. Drive it with deterministic tiny artifacts (a real saved optimiser JSON, a tiny .cbm/.rsglm or stubbed score_from_config) so optimiserApply/liveSwitch/modelScore/scenarioExpander are exercised, not skipped. Make it a required CI step in scripts/preflight.sh backend lane.
ci-prevention.prevents: Cluster C1 entirely: 'Generated liveSwitch body hard-wires live input', 'Generated optimiserApply body is a pure passthrough', 'Passthrough-body node types (optimiser/modelling/scenarioExpander/optimiserApply) no-op under standalone pipeline.run()'. Also any future codegen template that drifts from its executor builder (edge-join base/join role swap, constant/dataSource literal-vs-config drift).

ci-prevention.title: No registry invariant that every stateful NodeType shares one apply_*_from_config helper between codegen and executor
ci-prevention.location: src/haute/_registry.py (NODE_REGISTRY has exec+codegen+column_contract but no shared-runtime-helper slot); src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:784 (_make_passthrough_builder bypasses any shared helper)
ci-prevention.description: The architecture states the pricing math has ONE implementation: both _builders.py and _codegen_builders.py call apply_banding_from_config / apply_rating_step_from_config / score_from_config / execute_edge_join. But the passthrough node types (optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander) and liveSwitch are the exact set that DO NOT share a config-driven runtime helper -- codegen emits an inert body, the executor builder does the work. The registry already enforces 'exactly one exec AND one codegen builder per NodeType' (validate_registry_complete) and the codebase already uses the `set(declarations) == set(NodeType)` idiom in 4 places (test_chunk_plan, test_projection_planner, test_codegen_split, column contracts). The missing structural rule is: every NodeType that transforms data must route BOTH sides through a single shared apply_<type>_from_config(first, config, base_dir) entry point, so a no-op generated body becomes impossible to write.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: (1) Refactor each passthrough NodeType to a shared apply_*_from_config helper in graph_utils (apply_optimiser_apply_from_config, select_live_switch_input(source, **frames), etc.) called by both the exec builder and the codegen-emitted body. ci-prevention.prevents: Cluster C1 at the root (makes the divergence inexpressible, complementing Guard #1 which detects it). Future-proofs every new transform node against the same class.

ci-prevention.title: Frontend NodeType list (nodeTypes.ts / api/types.ts) is never mechanically checked against the backend NodeType enum
ci-prevention.location: frontend/src/utils/nodeTypes.ts:5-25 (NODE_TYPES); frontend/src/api/types.ts; src/haute/_types.py (NodeType enum); .github/workflows/ci.yml (backend + frontend are disjoint jobs)

A node type added/renamed on either side (e.g. a new transform node, or a value-string change) ships a frontend that can construct a node the backend rejects, or omits a palette entry, with zero CI signal. ci-prevention.prevents: Cluster C16/C17 drift class and frontend/backend enum desync generally; latent 'node type exists on one side only' bugs that currently have no test. Strengthens the wire-contract guarantee the architecture names as a defining obligation.

ci-prevention.title: JSON-shred conservation property exists for inference->shred but not for fingerprint-collision, $value/dotted-key collapse, or freshness identity
ci-prevention.location: tests/test_json_shred_properties.py:51-169 (emitted+skipped==visited, inference path only); src/haute/_json_shred.py:108-147 (_v2_fingerprint silent continue), :1199-1221 ($value collision), :1203/1213 (dotted-key path), _data_file_matches (mtime fast-path); src/haute/routes/json_cache.py
ci-prevention.description: There IS a strong conservation law for the inference->shred row path (every array element at an emitting depth is emitted-or-counted; emitted+skipped==visited). But the cluster-C2 bugs live at three boundaries that law does NOT cover: (1) _v2_fingerprint silently `continue`s past non-dict tables/columns so two structurally-different on-disk configs collapse to one schema_fingerprint and a stale cache is judged fresh (V015 $value-leaf drop, V016 dotted-key None-collapse are the same family -- a key literally named '$value' or containing '.' silently loses every record/value); (2) _data_file_matches returns fresh on (size, mtime_ns) WITHOUT hashing, so a byte-changing rewrite that preserves both serves stale; (3) the status/validity route reads the config WITHOUT validate_v2_schema. ci-prevention.prevents: Cluster C2 (all 5) plus V015 ($value collision silent table drop), V016 (dotted-key silent value loss). The named wave-2-cache-integrity concern.

ci-prevention.title: Rating-key Python-mirror vs Polars-twin property is strong but explicitly excludes the save-vs-apply dtype divergence and non-integer Float32

ci-prevention.description: This is the model guard the audit wants -- it canonicalises every value through BOTH normalise_rating_key and a real pl.Series/_rating_key_expr round trip, with a dtype grid. ci-prevention.prevents: Cluster C6 (both findings): normalise_rating_key vs _rating_key_expr Float32 disagreement; ratebook save-dtype vs apply-dtype silent neutral-1.0 miss.

ci-prevention.title: Fingerprint-COMPLETENESS is asserted ad hoc per cache, not as a single 'every output-affecting input is in the key' invariant
ci-prevention.location: src/haute/_cache.py (graph_fingerprint, canonical_json); src/haute/deploy/_schema.py (infer_output_schema keys on graph_fingerprint only); src/haute/_model_scorer.py (id(scoring_model)); _json_shred.py (schema_fingerprint); _cache.py:198-201,429-432 (non-injective node/extra-key joins V035)
ci-prevention.description: Clusters C3 + C11 + C12 + parts of C2/C16 share one root: a fingerprint omits an input class that changes the output (model-artifact bytes/version, preamble utility module resolved via sys.path, mtime ns-precision, duplicate-key handling) OR a join is non-injective (V035: node id / extra_key containing '|' or newline collides distinct graphs to one fingerprint; V034: NaN in a set makes canonical_json non-deterministic). These are tested, if at all, one cache at a time. There is no meta-property that, given a function producing a cache key, asserts perturbing ANY output-affecting input perturbs the key, and that the key encoder is injective under adversarial separators.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: (1) Injectivity property for canonical_json / graph_fingerprint: Hypothesis over node ids and extra_keys containing '|', '\n', and set/frozenset with NaN, asserting distinct logical inputs never collide and identical logical inputs always agree (kills V034, V035). (2) A 'fingerprint completeness' table-test: enumerate (cache_name, input_class) pairs (graph, file-bytes, model-artifact-bytes/version, preamble-module, categorical-levels); for each, mutate just that input and assert the relevant key changes -- a single registry of output-affecting inputs that every new cache must extend. This is the architecture's named 'fingerprint-COMPLETENESS dossier' as an executable gate.
ci-prevention.prevents: Clusters C3 (model-artifact/preamble/id-keyed), C11 (mtime ms-bucket), C12 (duplicate-key divergence), plus V034 (NaN-set non-determinism) and V035 (non-injective node/extra-key join). Stale-served-as-fresh across preview/trace/deploy.

ci-prevention.title: Deploy validate-vs-serve has no byte-identical-artifact assertion; the test-before-live gate can load a different model than the container serves

ci-prevention.title: Cross-language CI lanes never meet, and there is no contract-snapshot artifact shared between backend and frontend
ci-prevention.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-159 (backend, frontend, browser-e2e are independent jobs); scripts/preflight.sh:131-238 (RUN_BACKEND and RUN_FRONTEND disjoint)
ci-prevention.description: Backend and frontend correctness are validated in separate CI jobs and separate preflight branches. The only place they meet is browser-e2e (Playwright), which exercises rendered behaviour, not contract shape. Every wire-contract obligation the architecture names (api/types.ts <-> types/guards.ts, NodeType list, default-config shapes, cache-identity tokens like structuralVersion) is therefore validated only by hand-kept mirrors on each side. There is no generated contract snapshot that both sides assert against, so any of clusters C16/C17 (source-blind caches, under-keyed preview slots, WS sync identity) plus the frontend NodeType drift (separate finding) can land without a unit-level red.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Introduce a generated contract-snapshot step: backend emits a single contracts.json (NodeType values + per-type default config keys + wire field names + the cache-identity token contract) consumed by a frontend vitest that asserts the hand-written mirrors match. Add a dedicated 'contract-parity' CI job (or fold into both preflight lanes) so a contract change must update both sides in one PR. This makes the wire contract a tested artifact rather than a convention.
ci-prevention.prevents: Frontend/backend contract drift broadly; provides the harness home for the NodeType-parity guard and the structuralVersion/cache-identity agreement the architecture flags between client and backend.

ci-prevention.title: No guardrail forces new module-level mutable singletons to be test-isolated; conftest resets are reactive scars covering <40% of them
ci-prevention.location: tests/conftest.py:20-188 (11 autouse reset fixtures) vs. ~28 module-level mutable globals across src/haute/ (e.g. _model_scorer.py:77 _feature_validation_cache, _model_scorer.py:80 _feature_validation_last_entry, modelling/_feature_contract.py:266 _contract_cache, _mlflow_io.py:207 _model_cache, deploy/_scorer.py:81 _local_model_cache, execution.py:328 _runtime_path_fingerprint_memo, routes/_helpers.py:493 _pipeline_index, routes/_helpers.py:576 _module_deps, routes/_helpers.py:251 _self_write_paths, _sandbox.py:273 _validation_cache, server.py:493 _last_broadcast_fp)
ci-prevention.description: The conftest contains 11 hand-maintained autouse fixtures, each clearing one process-wide singleton, and every docstring admits it was added AFTER a specific leak (e.g. _clear_pipeline_dir_cache: 'without this, save tests delete real config files'; _clear_dual_cache_session: 'would let one test's working-layer state spill into another's emitter precedence check'). This is the reactive-patch anti-pattern: a leak is found in production-of-tests, a bespoke reset is bolted on, repeat. Crucially, a grep of src/haute shows ~28 mutable module-level globals (dicts/sets/caches/counters), but only ~11 are reset in conftest. The unguarded remainder (_feature_validation_cache, _contract_cache, _model_cache, _local_model_cache, _runtime_path_fingerprint_memo, _pipeline_index, _module_deps, _sandbox._validation_cache, etc.) are reset ONLY inside the single test file that exercises them locally -- so a leak originating in any OTHER test is invisible and order-dependent. This same state-bleed/stale-cache mechanism is the largest cluster in the audit catalog: findings 14 (size+mtime cache serves stale), 15 (preamble fingerprint stale), 34 (stale per-port parquet judged fresh), 36 (preview LRU keyed by nodeId alone), 40 (ms-bucket cache coarseness), 54 (_validation_cache keyed on id()), 60 (unbounded _validation_cache). The next such global added with no fixture will leak silently and only surface as a flaky, order-dependent failure under -n4 xdist.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a registry meta-test (tests/test_module_singleton_isolation.py) that AST-scans src/haute/ for module-level assignments whose value is a mutable container or known cache type (dict/set/list literals, Counter, WeakValueDictionary, FingerprintCache, LRUCache, StatGatedCache, lru_cache-decorated funcs, ContextVar) and asserts each is in one of two reviewed sets: (a) HAS_TEST_RESET -- a global with an exported _clear_*_for_tests/cache_clear/invalidate hook that conftest invokes autouse, or (b) EXEMPT -- documented immutable-after-import or per-request-scoped, with a one-line rationale. New globals fail CI until classified. Reuse the exact fingerprint-ratchet design already proven in tests/test_test_debt.py (path+scope+normalized-source SHA, _EXPECTED set, stale-by date). Pair it with a single conftest fixture that iterates a central RESETTABLE_SINGLETONS list calling each hook, replacing the 11 bespoke fixtures with one data-driven loop.
ci-prevention.prevents: The entire stale-cache / cross-test state-bleed class: catalog findings 14, 15, 34, 36, 40, 54, 60, plus every future module-global leak. Also prevents the recurring maintenance cost the 11 existing fixtures document.

ci-prevention.title: filterwarnings escalates only RuntimeWarning to error; Deprecation/Future/Resource/Pending warnings are swallowed, so silent dependency-drift and unclosed-resource bugs never fail CI
ci-prevention.location: pyproject.toml:148-152 (filterwarnings = ['error::RuntimeWarning', 'ignore:Mean of empty slice...', 'ignore:invalid value encountered in scalar divide...'])
ci-prevention.description: The warnings-as-errors policy is scoped to RuntimeWarning ONLY. DeprecationWarning, FutureWarning (which polars and pydantic emit aggressively across version bumps), ResourceWarning (unclosed files/sockets -- directly relevant given the catalog's leak findings 52 'cancelled fit leaks worker thread/Pool/train_dir' and 61 'PermissionError on Windows when a concurrent reader has the parquet open'), and PendingDeprecationWarning all pass silently. The project pins polars>=1.39,<2 and pydantic>=2.12,<3 with wide ranges; a minor bump that deprecates an API used on the pricing path produces a FutureWarning that no test will ever fail on, so the divergence ships. The two ignore-entries are unanchored substring filters (no module qualifier), so 'ignore:invalid value encountered in scalar divide' silences that RuntimeWarning from ANY library, not just the intended numeric kernel -- broader than necessary and could mask a genuine divide-by-zero in pricing math. There is no test asserting the filterwarnings policy itself (e.g. that the error:: escalation is present and the ignores are anchored).
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Escalate to 'error' as the default and downgrade specific, module-anchored exceptions: filterwarnings = ['error', 'ignore::DeprecationWarning:<third_party_module>', ...] with each ignore carrying a message+module qualifier and a comment naming the upstream issue. At minimum add 'error::DeprecationWarning:haute', 'error::FutureWarning', 'error::ResourceWarning' so first-party deprecations and unclosed resources fail. Anchor the two existing numeric ignores to their emitting module. Add a config meta-test asserting the policy contains an 'error' escalation for these categories (so a future PR can't quietly relax it), analogous to test_check_critical_coverage's gate-config validation.
ci-prevention.prevents: Silent polars/pydantic API drift on the pricing path (the 'two implementations diverge' class -- catalog 11/23/29/47/50), and unclosed-resource leaks (catalog 52, 61). Turns dependency upgrades into loud, fixable CI failures.

ci-prevention.title: A perf-named test that is not marked `perf` is collected by NEITHER lane and silently never runs
ci-prevention.location: scripts/run_perf_suite.py:226-241 (_build_pytest_args hardcodes '-m perf'); pyproject.toml:142 (addopts = "-m 'not perf'"); tests/test_scoring_prep_perf.py:536 and tests/test_cache_perf_fixes.py:709 mark only ONE function each, top-level files outside tests/performance/
ci-prevention.description: Perf coverage is partitioned by a single marker with no structural backstop. The default suite runs `-m 'not perf'` and the perf lane runs `-m perf`. A test that is perf-shaped (slow, benchmark-style) but where the author forgot @pytest.mark.perf -- or added a second perf function to test_scoring_prep_perf.py / test_cache_perf_fixes.py without remarking it (those files mark exactly one function each, not a module-level pytestmark like the tests/performance/ files use) -- is excluded from the perf lane AND, if it is slow, drags the default suite or gets caught by the 60s default timeout. Conversely the perf lane's _budget_violations correctly fails on zero-collected and on skips/xfails, but it cannot detect a perf test that was never marked, because collection never sees it. There is no guard that 'every test under tests/performance/ carries the perf marker' or 'every *_perf.py test function is marked perf', so the perf lane's breadth silently erodes -- the lane proves only that the marked subset is fast, never that the perf-relevant surface is the marked subset.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a structural test (extend test_performance_docs.py or a new test) that AST-scans tests/performance/**/*.py and tests/**/*_perf.py and asserts every test function/class is covered by the perf marker (module pytestmark or decorator). Optionally enforce the inverse: any test whose default-suite call-phase duration exceeds a threshold (already measured via --durations) must be either marked perf or marked slow -- a ratchet on the slowest-N. Standardise the two top-level perf files onto a module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.perf` to match tests/performance/.
ci-prevention.prevents: Silent perf-coverage erosion (a perf regression in an unmarked test is invisible) and accidental slow tests in the default lane. Complements the existing zero-collected guard which only fires when the WHOLE lane is empty.

ci-prevention.title: Mutation-target set covers 3 of ~18 critical-coverage modules; the highest-risk silent-divergence files have no mutation gate
ci-prevention.location: mutation/targets.json:3-22 (job-store, path-resolution, registry) vs pyproject.toml:170-287 (18 critical_coverage files); tests/test_mutation_suite_runner.py:28-47 pins exactly those 3
ci-prevention.description: Mutation testing -- the only gate that proves tests actually ASSERT behaviour rather than merely execute lines -- runs against just 3 modules. The critical_coverage config itself declares 18 files 'high-risk', and the audit catalog's worst findings live in modules with NO mutation target: executor.py (finding 19 duplicate-node-id collapse, 30 enforce_project_root=False arbitrary read), parser.py / _parser_regex.py / _parser_submodels.py (6 regex fallback drops submodels, 20 async nodes dropped, 21/22 submodel edge/overwrite loss), _model_scorer.py (24 predict_proba vs hard label, 54 id()-keyed cache), _json_shred.py (4 silent row inflation, 34 stale parquet judged fresh), _ram_estimate.py (31 ignores cgroup limits). These are precisely 'a mutated branch survives because no test asserts the consequence' bugs -- the class mutation testing exists to catch -- yet they are unmonitored. The test_mutation_suite_runner.py test hard-codes the 3-target set as correct, so the gap is frozen as intended rather than flagged as debt. The runner infrastructure (per-target thresholds, PR-smoke selection, manifest) is excellent; it is simply pointed at too little.

This makes the 15 uncovered critical modules visible, reviewed debt with a burn-down, instead of an invisible gap. Prioritise adding targets for executor.py, parser.py, and _model_scorer.py (the modules whose survivors map to the catalog's high-severity silent-divergence findings). Keep the bounded PR-smoke selection so wall-clock stays manageable.
ci-prevention.prevents: Silent-divergence / dropped-input bugs where lines are covered but no assertion exists (catalog 4, 6, 19, 20, 21, 22, 24, 30, 34) -- the exact class line-coverage cannot detect and mutation can.

ci-prevention.title: Critical-coverage ratchet has no anti-regression floor: thresholds can be silently lowered, and two files already encode a TODO/temporary loosening with no enforced burn-back
ci-prevention.location: scripts/check_critical_coverage.py (compares actual>=threshold but never compares threshold against a committed baseline); pyproject.toml:271-280 (optimiser.py rationale: 'TODO: ratchet back to 97/95'), pyproject.toml:259-262 (json_cache.py: 'restored to 90% (was temporarily lowered to 87%)')
ci-prevention.description: The gate enforces actual-coverage >= declared-threshold, but nothing enforces declared-threshold >= previously-declared-threshold. A PR that drops a file's min_branch_coverage from 95 to 80 to make a red build green passes every check (the gate, the meta-test test_check_critical_coverage, and preflight) with no signal that protection was weakened. The config already contains evidence this happens organically: optimiser.py was recalibrated down ('Recalibrated when the module grew ~4x') with a TODO to ratchet back that nothing enforces, and json_cache.py's comment records a prior temporary lowering to 87%. The user's own MEMORY explicitly flags 'No coverage gaming -- never lower the gate', yet the tooling permits exactly that. A ratchet whose only direction is documented-in-a-comment is not a ratchet. (Separately, threshold loosening is the gateway to the under-asserted-code class the mutation gap above also addresses.)
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a baseline-comparison test: store the current per-file thresholds as a committed snapshot (or read them from git HEAD/main) and fail if any min_statement_coverage or min_branch_coverage in pyproject.toml decreases relative to baseline without an explicit, dated, reviewed exemption entry. Encode any intentional temporary loosening (optimiser.py 97->95) as a dated debt entry with a burn-back deadline (mirror _DEBT_REVIEW_BY in test_test_debt) so a stale loosening fails CI after the date. This makes the ratchet monotonic-by-construction and turns the existing TODO comments into enforced obligations.
ci-prevention.prevents: Coverage-gaming via threshold relaxation (directly enforces the user's documented 'never lower the gate' rule) and the slow erosion of the under-asserted-code surface that feeds the silent-bug class.

ci-prevention.title: Process-wide singleton isolation is undefended against test-order and xdist sharding flakiness; no randomized-order or isolation-failure detection exists
ci-prevention.location: tests/conftest.py:20-188 (all isolation is autouse per-test reset within a worker); scripts/run_perf_suite.py / preflight.sh:165 (pytest -n "$PYTEST_WORKERS" with default ordering, no -p randomly)
ci-prevention.description: Every isolation fixture clears state per-test, which only protects against leakage when the NEXT test runs in the same worker. The suite runs under xdist (-n4) which sharded by file, so the de-facto execution order is stable-but-arbitrary and differs from a serial run. Two failure modes are undetected: (1) a singleton with no reset fixture (see Finding 1) leaks within a worker and produces an order-dependent pass/fail that is reproducible only under one specific shard assignment -- invisible until an unrelated PR reshuffles files across workers; (2) a fixture that clears BEFORE but not AFTER (or vice-versa) leaves a window. The catalog's flaky-by-shared-state findings (54 id()-keyed cache collision, 60 unbounded accumulation, 40 ms-bucket collision) are exactly the shape that randomized ordering surfaces. There is no scheduled job that runs the suite with -p randomly (random seed) or with --forked, so cross-test contamination has no detector; it is found only when it breaks main.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Add a scheduled (weekly, like mutation/perf) CI leg that runs the full backend suite with pytest-randomly (random order, logged seed) AND a second pass with -p no:cacheprovider + a fresh worker-per-test or --forked sampling on the highest-risk modules. A failure means a real isolation bug; the logged seed makes it reproducible. This is the dynamic complement to Finding 1's static registry: the registry prevents un-isolated globals; the randomized run catches isolation logic that is present but wrong (clear-before-only, missing teardown).
ci-prevention.prevents: Order-dependent flakiness from shared-state contamination (catalog 40, 54, 60) and broken-but-present isolation fixtures; surfaces leaks before they hit main rather than after a file-shuffle exposes them.

ci-prevention.title: conftest globally monkeypatches StarletteTestClient.__init__ and httpx.AsyncClient.__init__ for every test, a broad autouse mutation of third-party class internals with no scoping or contract test
ci-prevention.location: tests/conftest.py:35-75 (_local_session_auth_for_route_clients autouse, monkeypatch.setattr on StarletteTestClient.__init__ and httpx.AsyncClient.__init__)
ci-prevention.description: An autouse fixture rewrites the constructors of two third-party HTTP-client classes for the entire suite to inject a session token and rewrite base_url from testserver->localhost. This is a global behavioural override of library internals applied to tests that may have nothing to do with route auth. Risks: (1) it silently changes base_url for any AsyncClient using ASGITransport at testserver, which can mask a test that intended to assert default-URL behaviour; (2) it couples every test to Starlette/httpx private __init__ signatures -- an httpx minor bump that changes __init__ kwargs breaks the whole suite at once with an opaque error, not just auth tests; (3) being autouse, it grants ambient authentication, so a test cannot easily verify the UNauthenticated 401 path without extra effort, weakening coverage of the security boundary (related to catalog 30's auth-boundary concerns). It is the kind of 'convenience global' the codebase's own anti-fallback principle warns against.
ci-prevention.recommended_guard: Convert to an explicit, named fixture (e.g. authed_client) that route tests opt into, leaving a separate fixture for unauthenticated probes -- making auth an explicit dimension of each test rather than ambient. If a global default must remain, add a contract test that constructs a bare httpx.AsyncClient/TestClient and asserts the patched signature still accepts the expected kwargs, so an httpx/starlette bump fails with a clear, localized message instead of cascading across the suite.
ci-prevention.prevents: Suite-wide opaque breakage on httpx/starlette upgrades, and under-tested unauthenticated/401 security paths (supports catalog 30). Reduces hidden coupling to library internals.

dependencies.detail: `fastapi>=0.129.0,<0.130` transitively caps starlette at 0.52.x. The starlette CVE fixes that matter (host-spoof, StaticFiles, urlencoded limit bypass) land in starlette>=1.0.1/1.1.0/1.3.1, which fastapi 0.129 does not allow. So the single most security-relevant upper bound in pyproject is currently blocking the starlette patches.
dependencies.recommendation: Do NOT widen the fastapi bound ad hoc (starlette 1.x is a breaking change for fastapi). Plan a coordinated bump to a fastapi release that depends on starlette>=1.3 as a follow-up; until then rely on haute's existing mitigations (loopback default bind, LocalTrustedHostMiddleware Host validation, request.url.path-only usage, is_relative_to static guard). Add a regression test asserting the server rejects spoofed Host headers and that form-field limits are enforced for urlencoded bodies (the CVE-2026-54283 gap) so a future starlette bump is verified.

dependencies.detail: Two DIRECT core deps ship vulnerable floors that have free in-range fixes: `python-multipart>=0.0.22,<0.1` (fix 0.0.31 is < 0.1) and `python-dotenv>=1.2.1,<2` (fix 1.2.2 is < 2). The upper bounds are fine; only the resolved/lower versions are stale.
dependencies.recommendation: Raise the lower pins to `python-multipart>=0.0.31,<0.1` and `python-dotenv>=1.2.2,<2` (or just `uv lock --upgrade-package python-multipart --upgrade-package python-dotenv`). These are the only DIRECT-dependency security fixes and both are zero-risk within existing bounds.

dependencies.detail: cryptography (46.0.7), idna (3.15), pyasn1 (0.6.3), requests (2.33.0), urllib3 (2.7.0) all have fixes with NO blocking upper bound in pyproject (they are unpinned transitives) but the lock is pinned to older versions.
dependencies.recommendation: Run `uv lock --upgrade` to refresh the transitive graph, then re-run pip-audit to confirm the count drops. Low risk; defense-in-depth. Most of these only ship under the databricks extra anyway.

dependencies.detail: The entire mlflow/databricks stack (mlflow x8, pyjwt x11, gitpython x4, flask, werkzeug, mako, cryptography x5, pyasn1, plus heavy transitives: alembic, docker, graphene/graphql, sqlalchemy via alembic, gunicorn-free flask server) is pulled ONLY by the optional `databricks` extra. It is, however, force-installed in dependency-groups.dev via `haute[databricks]`, so every developer/CI env resolves the full vulnerable set even though production installs without the extra are clean.
dependencies.recommendation: Keep mlflow/databricks strictly optional (good current design). Consider a CI matrix split: run the default security audit against the CORE dependency set (no extra) to reflect the real shipped attack surface, and a separate informational audit with the databricks extra. This makes the audit count honest about what end users actually install (core: only starlette/python-multipart/python-dotenv/idna are vulnerable).

dependencies.detail: pillow (12MB+, 6 CVEs) and the matplotlib stack reach the CORE install via catboost->matplotlib, but haute imports NO matplotlib/PIL and never plots or decodes images. matplotlib is also pulled by mlflow. It is effectively dead weight on the core runtime that nonetheless contributes 6 CVEs to the audit headline.
dependencies.recommendation: Confirm catboost cannot be installed without matplotlib (it is a hard dep of catboost, so it cannot be trimmed without dropping catboost). Since the image code is unreachable, treat all pillow CVEs as non-issues but document the rationale so future audits don't re-triage them. No action needed beyond letting pillow float to 12.2.0 on lock refresh.

dependencies.detail: AGPL-3.0-only project. Reviewed the resolved dependency set: fastapi/starlette/pydantic/uvicorn/click/orjson/pillow (MIT/HPND), polars (MIT), catboost/mlflow/databricks-sdk/databricks-sql-connector/cryptography/protobuf (Apache-2.0), gitpython/joblib/numpy/prettytable/lz4/pyasn1 (BSD), pyjwt (MIT). No GPL-2.0-only (incompatible-with-AGPLv3-as-licensee-imposed), no commercial/proprietary, and no SSPL/BUSL packages observed in the lock.
dependencies.recommendation: No license conflict for distribution under AGPL-3.0-only: all dependencies are permissive (MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0/HPND) which AGPLv3 may incorporate. Note Apache-2.0 is one-way compatible INTO (A)GPLv3 (fine here). Keep an eye that no future dep introduces GPL/AGPL-incompatible terms; a periodic `pip-licenses`/`uv`-based license scan in CI would make this a guardrail rather than a manual check.

dependencies.runtime_exposure: NOT shipped to browser. @babel/core runs at BUILD time (JSX/React transform). The file-read requires compiling attacker-controlled source containing a crafted sourceMappingURL; inputs are first-party app source. UNREACHABLE; lowest priority.
dependencies.recommended_action: `npm update @babel/core` to the patched 7.x. Optionally align the directly-pinned @babel/parser/traverse/types to the same patched minor for consistency.

dependencies.detail: All entries in dependencies and devDependencies use EXACT pins (no ^ or ~), e.g. react 19.2.4, vite 6.3.5, vitest 4.0.18. This is good supply-chain hygiene (reproducible installs) and is backed by package-lock.json + a committed bun.lock. The float only exists in transitive ranges inside the lockfile.
dependencies.recommendation: Keep exact pins. When applying the security bumps, update BOTH the exact pin in package.json AND regenerate package-lock.json (and bun.lock) so the two lockfiles stay consistent.

dependencies.detail: Both frontend/package-lock.json (npm; CI uses `npm ci`) and frontend/bun.lock (bun) are committed. The audit and CI are npm-based. Divergence between the two could mean a `bun install` resolves different transitive versions than CI audits.
dependencies.recommendation: Treat package-lock.json as the source of truth for CI/audit. After security bumps, regenerate bun.lock in the same change (or document that bun is not the supported install path) to avoid drift between the two resolved trees.

dependencies.detail: Checked the suspicious-looking devDeps. @babel/parser, @babel/traverse, @babel/types (pinned 7.29.0) are NOT unused: they are imported by frontend/scripts/check-ui-dependencies.mjs and the AST architecture-guard tests (src/__tests__/hover/previewPanelsHover.test.tsx, editorsHover.test.tsx). elkjs 0.11.0 is used by src/utils/layout.ts (graph auto-layout) and ships to the browser legitimately. lucide-react is used across ~30 components. No dead production or dev dependency identified.
dependencies.recommendation: No removal needed. (If desired, run `npx depcheck` / `knip` as a periodic CI hygiene gate, but current manifest is clean.)

dependencies.detail: Heaviest shipped deps are the @codemirror/* family (8 packages: autocomplete/commands/lang-python/language/lint/search/state/view) plus @lezer grammars, @xyflow/react 12.10.0 (React Flow), elkjs 0.11.0 (ELK layout engine, large WASM/JS), and react/react-dom 19. The vite config already code-splits these into dedicated manual chunks (vendor-react, vendor-layout=elkjs, vendor-codemirror, vendor-ui=lucide-react), and the repo has check-bundle-size.mjs + analyze-bundle-sourcemaps.mjs guards. elkjs is the single largest non-React bundle contributor.
dependencies.recommendation: No action required for security. For bundle weight, the existing manualChunks + check:bundle gate is the right control; keep elkjs and codemirror lazy/chunked. None of these shipped deps have advisories.

dependencies.detail: Project is AGPL-3.0. Every package in the affected (vulnerable) paths is MIT-licensed (@babel/core MIT, js-yaml MIT, postcss MIT, undici MIT, vite MIT, vitest MIT, jsdom MIT). The shipped dependency set (react, @xyflow/react, @codemirror/*, elkjs, lucide-react, zustand, tailwindcss) is MIT/ISC/permissive.
